claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy coating can be successfully applied and adhered to a Cu matrix.
A tungsten-based RHEA coating will enhance the wear resistance of Cu.
The high hardness and thermal stability of a tungsten-based RHEA provide protection under severe frictional conditions.
A tungsten-based RHEA can be prepared in powder or thin-film form by methods such as selective laser melting or sputtering.
Controlled deposition can minimize thermal stresses and promote bonding between a W-Ta or W-Cr RHEA and Cu.
Deposition will form a dense, high-hardness interfacial layer between the Cu substrate and the RHEA coating.
The interfacial layer will provide good adhesion and chemical bonding while accommodating thermal-expansion mismatch.
The high-entropy effect in a refractory alloy produces a stable solid solution with superior hardness and wear resistance.
Tungsten contributes a high melting point and oxidation resistance to the coating.
The tungsten-containing coating protects the relatively soft Cu substrate.
Minor interdiffusion during processing can improve coating adhesion and load transfer.
RHEAs possess excellent mechanical properties at elevated temperatures.
Compared with bare Cu, RHEA-coated Cu will show a significant reduction in wear rate.
Compared with bare Cu, RHEA-coated Cu will show a significant reduction in coefficient of friction.
RHEA-coated Cu will maintain structural integrity under variable-temperature conditions.
Thermal-expansion mismatch can limit coating success by impairing adhesion or mechanical performance.
Brittle intermetallic compounds may form and impair coating or interface performance.
Inadequate deposition-process control can impair adhesion and mechanical performance.
The chemical interactions at the tungsten-based RHEA/Cu interface are not fully established.
The long-term durability of the coating under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading is not fully established.
